bullets.title: August NFP blowout (+162K) shifts Fed hike odds above 50% for Sep 16
bullets.body: August nonfarm payrolls came in at +162K vs. 55K consensus, with July revised from -23K to +21K and a 3-month average of +71K; unemployment held at 4.1%. The employment diffusion index hit a 2-year high at 55.6% and manufacturing diffusion hit a 4-year high at 61.1%. September FOMC hike odds rose to 58–64% post-print, with the September 11 CPI print now the decisive catalyst. Wages at +0.27% m/m kept inflation hawks from claiming a clear win, with Morgan Stanley, Wolfe, and Hedgeye each interpreting the print differently—from hawkish to mixed to Quad 2 confirming.

bullets.title: Global central banks in synchronized tightening: ECB hike 'done deal,' BoJ hiking twice by year-end
bullets.body: JPMorgan, UBS, and Citi all converged on the ECB delivering a September hike (to 2.5%) with a third hike in December likely; eurozone headline inflation at 3.26% driven by energy (TTF 50%+ above June ECB assumption), core at 2.41%. BoJ hiking in September and December to 1.5% per JPMorgan—"virtually certain." Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech set the tone: 2% PCE is a firm target, financial conditions are not restrictive, and more work may be needed.

bullets.title: September rate-hike setup is 'Good News is Bad News': JPM turns Tactically Cautious/Neutral
bullets.body: JPM's trading desk shifted to Tactically Cautious/Neutral, flagging choppy positioning, post-Labor Day credit spread widening risk, September's historically worst seasonal, and a Momentum factor down 21–34% from June highs (outside typical 10–15% drawdowns). The desk recommends reducing net-longs, adopting dollar-neutral positioning for 2–3 weeks, and preferring Mag7 over AI/Memory/Semis near-term, with large-cap banks and Consumer Discretionary favored if energy prices fall.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury yield hits 4.75–4.80%, multi-month highs; global bond yields at multi-decade peaks
bullets.body: US 10-year yields broke above 4.74% cycle highs and tested 4.80%, while Germany's 30-year bund hit levels last seen in 2011. Drivers: Warsh's hawkish r-star commentary, the Iran-US conflict lifting oil to $85–91/bbl, and AI capex issuance crowding Treasury demand. JPM's US Treasury desk recommended selling the 20-year sector as 2bp rich vs. the 10s/30s butterfly. 22V and others note that 6%+ nominal GDP makes material yield relief unlikely absent supply shocks easing.

bullets.title: Oil surges to $85–91/bbl on Iran-US military escalation; Strait of Hormuz risk elevated
bullets.body: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers; Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles at US bases in Jordan and Kuwait. Brent broke above $90, diesel crack spreads approached $100/bbl, and European TTF gas spiked to highest since January 2023. Piper Sandler raised 3Q Brent to $88 and Morgan Stanley raised 4Q WTI to $96. 22V and JPM Energy Shock Monitor tracked tanker flows well below pre-conflict levels, with US SPR at 44-year lows. The conflict is the primary driver of ECB September hike odds and Warsh's hawkish posture.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Hugging Face for ~$13B, invests $3.5B in MediaTek convertible bonds
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed a $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face (plus $1B retention), its largest-ever deal, securing the leading open-source AI platform with 18M+ developers. Separately, NVIDIA invested $3.5B in MediaTek convertible bonds and deepened collaboration via NVLink Fusion, expanding the custom ASIC ecosystem beyond traditional GPU customers. Both moves reinforce NVIDIA's strategy of controlling the AI software/distribution layer alongside hardware dominance.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure AI capex narrative accelerates: AVGO guides FY28 AI revenue to $230B, DELL raises FY27 to $192B
bullets.body: Broadcom guided FY27 AI semiconductor revenue to $115B (up from $100B) and FY28 to $230B (~double again), with Anthropic set to become the largest XPU customer. Six hyperscalers are committed; supply constraints (wafers, substrates, HBM) are the primary limiter. Dell raised FY27 guidance to $192B revenue (+70% YoY) and $74B AI server revenue, with $95B backlog and $60.9B new orders. HPE raised FY27 revenue growth to 13–17% on a $3.5B hyperscale inferencing deal and gigawatt-scale Oracle switching.

bullets.title: Semis rotation from hardware to software accelerates; High Beta Momentum factor down 77% since June
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Macro Show and GS QDS both flagged the GS High Beta Momentum basket (long Semis/short Software) declining 77% from June highs. The reverse trade—AI Software Long vs. Semis Short—was up 18% in August. SOX index was 22% off its June peak and below its downward-sloping 50-day MA. 22V, Citi, and MS all noted software benefiting from reduced AI-disruption fears (a16z 'System-of-Record' thesis), with IGV up 17% in August (best month in 2 years).

bullets.title: SNOW blowout: product revenue accelerates to 37% YoY, FY27 raised to 36% growth
bullets.body: Snowflake's Q2 product revenue beat by 5%+ at $1.49B (+37% YoY), the third consecutive quarter of acceleration. AI products (CoCo/CoWork) contributed ~half the acceleration. FY27 product revenue guidance raised to $6.07B (+36% YoY), implying 40%+ growth potential in H2. Q3 guidance implied 37–38% YoY. NRR stable at 126%. Multiple analysts raised PTs sharply: Citi to $490, UBS to $500, KeyBanc to $460, Wolfe to $500.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: Tech/Software net bought; Real Estate net sold at fastest pace in 7 months
bullets.body: Goldman Prime Services reported Info Tech, Comm Services, and Financials as most net bought sectors for the week, while Real Estate was net sold for the fourth straight week at the fastest pace in nearly 7 months (-2.3 SDs). US L/S net leverage at 48.4% (4th percentile 1-year). Gross leverage rose to 208.5% (27th percentile). Fundamental L/S managers were down 0.55% on the week, driven by short-side losses, while Systematic L/S gained +1.67%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 up 0.1% for the week, +12.8% YTD; August ended +2.62% led by software and Mag7
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed the week up just 0.09%, with Nasdaq +0.40%. August was a stronger month at +2.62% for the S&P, led by software (IGV +16.3%) and Mag7. Weekly standouts included SNDK +17.2%, HOOD +17.1%, and DELL +14.9%, while CIEN fell 15.2% and PINS dropped 12%. S&P earnings beat rate for Q2 was exceptional—Jefferies noted SPX EPS growth on pace for ~35% vs ~15% initial expectations, with 6 consecutive quarters of 75%+ guidance affirmations.

bullets.title: Jefferies and GS bullish on corporate earnings momentum; 70%+ of S&P 500 companies maintained or raised guidance
bullets.body: Jefferies flagged the R3K 1FY EPS guidance revision ratio hitting 7+ for the first time outside recession/tax reform comparisons, with 70%+ of S&P companies maintaining or raising Q-EPS guidance and 40% outright raising. Record 6th consecutive quarter with 75%+ of SPX affirming or raising sales guidance. GS flagged SPX EPS growth of +51% YoY in Q2 (largely from hyperscaler equity stake gains—Anthropic valuation surge drove $150B+ in 'other income' for GOOGL and AMZN).

bullets.title: S&P 500 index rebalance: ANET, DELL, SNDK added to S&P 100; BE, ILMN join S&P 500
bullets.body: S&P Global announced changes effective September 21, 2026: ANET, DELL, PANW, and SNDK added to S&P 100; Bloom Energy (BE) and Illumina (ILMN) join the S&P 500; HUBS, AGNC, and others move into the S&P MidCap 400. Changes coincide with the quarterly rebalance.

bullets.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra; achieves 99.9 on ARC-AGI-3, cuts task costs 50%
bullets.body: OpenAI released Astra, which scored 62.7% on ARC-AGI-3 benchmarks (vs. 30.2% for Opus) and was trained on a 100K GPU cluster. CEO Sam Altman declared the AGI era has begun. The model reduces coding task costs >50%, posing concerns for AI-native companies reliant on per-token revenue. ChatGPT's ad business separately hit $1B annualized revenue run rate, with OpenAI rolling out self-serve ads globally. GS described Astra as a breakthrough that 'revitalizes AI spending necessity.'

bullets.title: EDA stocks flash-crashed on OpenAI Astra PCB demo before bouncing; Mizuho says selloff unwarranted
bullets.body: SNPS fell 7% and CDNS 5% after OpenAI released a video of GPT-6 Astra performing PCB layout in KiCad—a common manual engineering bottleneck. Mizuho argued the demo mirrors the Kimi K3 episode: Astra is orchestrating existing open-source KiCad tools, not replacing EDA engines. SNPS does not compete in PCB layout authoring. Agentic AI automating manual steps could drive greater EDA engine utilization, not displacement.

bullets.title: CPI (Sep 11) is the decisive catalyst for the September 16 FOMC meeting, not NFP
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks—JPM, Piper Sandler, Wolfe, and 22V—all emphasized that August CPI (releasing Sep 11) is more critical than the NFP beat for determining the September 16 FOMC decision. Fed Governor Waller explicitly said he would hold if core CPI is ≤0.3% m/m (he would hike if it's higher). Morgan Stanley models core CPI at 0.23% m/m and core PCE at ~0.20%, which would support a hold. Inflation nowcasts from Hedgeye put August CPI at +3.50% YoY.

bullets.title: AI data center buildout faces new NIMBY/regulatory headwinds ahead of midterms
bullets.body: Texas, Pennsylvania, Ohio, and New York (state-wide moratorium) tightened data center regulatory requirements in August. Trump countered by urging communities to embrace data centers for jobs and taxes. GS TMT, 22V, and Mizuho all noted peak NIMBY concern likely ahead of November midterms before a year-end rally. Power/grid interconnection delays are real constraints alongside political opposition; EQIX and DLR's entitled, in-progress projects provide a buffer.

bullets.title: Anthropic's $35–80B compute deals set new pricing floor at $16M/MW/year
bullets.body: Anthropic signed two six-year compute deals totaling $80B: $35B with Nvidia-backed Lambda (at HUT8's Texas Beacon Point AI campus) and a separate $45B deal. Bitdeer's 9MW Asia deal confirmed $16M/MW/year pricing across counterparties—60% above prior $10M/MW/year historical norms. Six-year terms signal confidence in GPU longevity. 22V noted this pricing as bullish for CRWV and NBIS revenue.

bullets.title: California wildfire legislation fails utilities; PCG -20%, EIX -26% in August
bullets.body: California's SB 492 failed to inject new capital, establish an evergreen fund, or break the link between fund solvency and shareholder liability. Mizuho, Wells Fargo, BMO, and Truist all downgraded PCG and EIX. PCG launched a strategic business review and deferred ~$2B in investment. Jefferies, Goldman, and Wolfe Research estimated 10–15% additional downside risk from current levels. SRE least exposed given Texas/LNG mix.
